commit.message:
feat(security): assert TLS cipher suites on the AD LDAPS hop, via a proved-equivalent replica context (BACKLOG #1317 partial, ADR 0180) (#671)

* feat(auth): assert the AD LDAPS hop's TLS suites (BACKLOG #1317)

The #1317 core landed in ae72f5828 / 4e9bf38de and its row states the
remainder exactly: ldap3, hvac and ODBC Driver 18 "choose their own suites
and no engine object exists to assert on". This closes the ldap3 half.

Measured with one instrument on two real call sites: the HTTP-family opener
reached harden_cipher_suites 1 time while LdapAuthenticator._server() reached
it 0. Arm A proves the spy fires, so Arm B's zero is a missing call and not a
dead instrument. An ldap3.Tls carries ZERO SSLContext attributes -- it builds
the context inside wrap_socket at connect time and exposes no ssl_context= to
inject one through, so the engine can never hold the object this hop uses.

The suite list that hop resolves to is CLEAN today (17 suites, zero NULL, zero
anonymous, zero non-forward-secret, at both ad_tls_verify settings). So the
defect is inheritance without assertion -- the class harden_cipher_suites'
docstring names -- not a negotiable weak suite. Severity conditional per
CLAUDE.md section 0: nothing is intercepted today; a deploying site WOULD
cross an unasserted context on its AD bind.

assert_ldap3_tls_suites rebuilds ldap3's construction and asserts that. Since
identity is unavailable here, two measurements stand in for it: a test drives
ldap3's REAL wrap_socket over a socketpair, captures the SSLContext off the
resulting SSLSocket and requires its suite list to equal the replica's; and
_tls_kwargs() is the single definition both __init__ and _server() read, with
a test requiring what was asserted to be what the bind uses.

It REFUSES any Tls argument it cannot reproduce. ldap3/core/tls.py wraps
set_ciphers in `except ssl.SSLError: pass`, so routing suite policy through
Tls(ciphers=...) is a measured trap: a rejected string is swallowed and the
TLS 1.2 list drops from 14 suites to 0 with nothing reported. The refusal
turns that into a loud construction-time error.

Asserted once at construction, not per call: the answer is fixed by config,
AuthService builds this eagerly, and _server() runs up to three times per
login. ca_certs_file is accepted and deliberately not loaded -- measured, it
changes the trust anchors and not one entry of the suite list.

Red-first: test_ad_ldaps_bind_asserts failed DID NOT RAISE ValueError before
the wiring. Five mutations each red a distinct test, all files restored
byte-identical; deleting the call reds two tests while drifting _server() off
_tls_kwargs() reds only the argument test.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(adr): ADR 0180 -- asserting TLS suites where a library exposes no context (BACKLOG #1317)

Records the decision behind the #1317 remainder, and scopes the two libraries
the row names alongside ldap3 rather than leaving them open by implication.

The general question is non-obvious and sets precedent: where a library
exposes no SSLContext, assert a REBUILT one and pin the rebuild by capturing
the library's own, and REFUSE any argument the rebuild cannot reproduce. The
precedent is deliberately narrow -- where the library's context IS reachable,
assert it, because substituting a look-alike silently changed ALPN and
post-handshake auth when that was tried on the urllib hops.

Scopes the other two OUT with measurements rather than deferring them:

hvac is not assertable from these modules today and is recorded as
concluded-as-research. hvac, requests and urllib3 are all absent from the
interpreter, hvac is pinned but never installed, and NO CI leg installs the
[vault] extra (measured across .github/workflows/, which installs
dev,harness,fhir,dicom,x12,xml,webauthn plus sqlserver/postgres). A control
there would be one no test in this project can execute -- the silent-control
shape ADR 0158 catalogues. Also corrects the row's scope: there are THREE hvac
clients, not two, because crypto_transit.py imports _build_client from
keyprovider_vault, so two construction points cover all three. Names what
would change the answer: the extra on a CI leg, then assert through urllib3's
own create_urllib3_context rather than a hand-rolled look-alike.

ODBC Driver 18 is out permanently, not deferred. store/sqlserver.py contains
no ssl usage at all; TLS is connection-string keywords (Encrypt,
TrustServerCertificate, ServerCertificate) terminated inside the native
driver, so there is no Python-side context to assert and no replica is
possible -- the suite list belongs to the driver and the OS TLS stack.

Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* docs(backlog): record on #1317 what this PR actually lands

The required check "a PR that implements BACKLOG #N must update BACKLOG.md"
was red: this branch cites #1317 and changes engine code without touching the
ledger. That check exists to catch exactly this, so the fix is the row, not a
bypass.

This is an EDIT to an existing row, not a new one, so it is committable from a
worktree that did not allocate #1317 -- the same property that let the banner
flips land earlier today.

The row stays PARTIAL and its banner does not flip. What shipped is one call
site gaining a cipher assertion; the strict positive allowlist the row asks for
is still unbuilt.

parse_items before and after: 395 items both sides, none added, none removed,
#1317 still open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

---------

Co-authored-by: wshallwshall <mefordev@messagefoundry.org>
Co-authored-by: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
